title: Factors, multiples, primes
examples: When should I use a divisibility rule?
What is the difference between a factor and a multiple?
How do I check if a big number is prime?

explain.say: Today we will learn about factors and multiples. Say a factor is a number that divides another number exactly. Say for example, the factors of twelve are one, two, three, four, six, and twelve.

Next we look at factor pairs. Say a factor pair is two numbers that multiply together to give a target number. Say for the number twelve, the factor pairs are one and twelve, two and six, and three and four.

items: The product equals the target number

explain.say: Now we test for prime numbers. Say a prime number is a whole number greater than one with exactly two factors. Say the number seven is prime because its only factors are one and seven.
We can use divisibility rules to check easily. Say to check if a number is divisible by three, you add up its digits. Say if the sum is divisible by three, the whole number is too.

items: Sum of digits must be divisible by 3

faq.q: What is the smallest prime number?
faq.a: The smallest prime number is two. Say remember that one is not a prime number because it only has one factor.
asks: What is the first prime number?

faq.q: How do I find all the factors of a large number?
faq.a: You can systematically check every number starting from one up to the square root of that number. Say if it divides evenly, it is a factor.
asks: What is the best way to find factors?
Do I check up to the number itself?

faq.q: What is the difference between a square number and a cube number?
faq.a: A square number is a number multiplied by itself, like four times four. Say a cube number is a number multiplied by itself three times, like two times two times two.
asks: How is a cube different from a square?

faq.q: If a number is divisible by two, what else can I say about it?
faq.a: If a number is divisible by two, it means the number is even. Say all even numbers end in zero, two, four, six, or eight.
asks: What does it mean to be divisible by two?
Are all even numbers divisible by two?

faq.q: Do all prime numbers have to be odd?
faq.a: No, the number two is a prime number, and it is even. Say two is the only even prime number.
asks: Is two prime or not prime?
Can an even number be prime?

facts: A factor of a number is a number that divides it exactly.
Prime numbers only have two factors: one and themselves.
A square number is the result of multiplying a whole number by itself.
A cube number is the result of multiplying a whole number by itself three times.

quiz.say: Which number is a factor of thirty-six?
quiz.why: Four divides thirty-six exactly because thirty-six divided by four equals nine.

wrong.0: Five is tempting because thirty-six ends in six, but it is not divisible by five.
wrong.1: Seven is tempting because it is a small prime number, but thirty-six divided by seven leaves a remainder.
wrong.2: Ten is tempting because it ends in zero, but thirty-six is not a multiple of ten.

quiz.why: Twenty-nine is prime because its only factors are one and twenty-nine. Say it cannot be divided evenly by any smaller number.

wrong.1: Thirty-three is wrong because it is divisible by three and eleven.
wrong.2: Thirty-five is wrong because it ends in five, so it is divisible by five.
wrong.3: Twenty-seven is wrong because it is a cube number, divisible by three and nine.

quiz.say: What is the smallest number that is both a square and a cube?
quiz.why: Sixty-four is the smallest number that can be written as a square and a cube. Say it is eight times eight, and also four times four times four.

wrong.0: Twelve is wrong because it is not a perfect square or a perfect cube.
wrong.1: Thirty-six is wrong because it is a square, but it is not a perfect cube.
wrong.2: One hundred is wrong because while it is a square, it is not the smallest number that fits both rules.
